items.body: هل يرحل المدرب اليوناني؟ كشف صحفي سعودي عن حقيقة الأنباء التي تشير إلى إمكانية إقالة اليوناني جورجوس دونيس، المدير الفني للمنتخب السعودي، بعد تأجيل بطولة كأس أمم آسيا 2027. وأعلن الاتحاد الآسيوي لكرة القدم، صباح أول أمس الثلاثاء، تأجيل بطولة كأس أمم آسيا التي كان من المُقرر انطلاقها في يناير/كانون الثاني 2027، لتُقام بدءًا من ديسمبر/كانون الأول من نفس العام. وقالت تقارير صحفية إن الاتحاد السعودي لكرة القدم يفكر في إقالة دونيس، والتعاقد مع مدير فني جديد لقيادة المنتخب الأول خلال بطولة كأس أمم آسيا 2027 نهاية العام المقبل. غير أن الصحفي السعودي بدر الصقري نفى تلك الأنباء، في تصريحات لبرنامج "نادينا" على قناة "MBC 1". تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشتر تذكرتك الآن! وقال الصقري في هذا الصدد: "تواصلت مع مسؤولين في الاتحاد السعودي لكرة القدم لسؤالهم عن مستقبل دونيس، وجاء الرد بأنهم لا يفكرون إطلاقًا في إقالته من منصبه". وأضاف: "لا يوجد تفكير من قبل الاتحاد السعودي لكرة القدم في التعاقد مع جهاز فني جديد، وسيكون ذلك دربًا من الجنون إن حدث، وفقًا لتصريحات المصدر المسؤول نفسه". وأتم: "أكد المسؤولون على أن دونيس سيكون مستمرًا مع المنتخب السعودي في البطولة الآسيوية، وبالتالي لن تكون هناك مشكلة في تجديد العقد الذي ينتهي قبل بدايتها لمدة عام إضافي". ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديا…

items.title: Uranium cubes reveal why the German nuclear project failed
items.summary: "Our calculations suggest Heisenberg significantly underestimated the materials required."
items.body: During World War II, physicists on the Manhattan Project worried that the Nazi German nuclear program might achieve the first nuclear bomb before the US and its allies. That's not what transpired, but historians have debated just how close the Germans came to achieving criticality in their last attempt at building a reactor: the B8 pile. Werner Heisenberg, who led that effort, claimed that they were close and had only needed a little more uranium. But according to a paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus, that was not the case: the project simply didn't have sufficient uranium and heavy water to build a working bomb, given the design they were using. This particular research started in 2013, when University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth—a co-author on the new paper—received the gift of a mysterious heavy metal cube from a friend. He instantly recognized it as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists in their unsuccessful attempt to build a working nuclear reactor. Only 14 such cubes are known to exist today. items.body: After alienating many long-time small- to medium-sized business (SMB) customers, Broadcom’s VMware is trying to appeal to its smaller customers. Today, the virtualization company announced vSphere Express, a lower-end virtualization offering for organizations that require “cost-effective essential virtualization.” vSphere Express comes after many customers reported that VMware was pushing them to VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), the flagship private cloud bundle that has many features SMBs don’t need and is expensive. items.title: AMD's record quarter: Data center business doubles, while gaming craters
items.summary: AMD's gaming revenue fell 40 percent in an otherwise record $13.4 billion quarter.
items.body: AMD reported third-quarter revenues on Tuesday with a record $13.4 billion, an increase of 45 percent year over year, as data center business nearly doubled and the company's gaming segment cratered. AMD CFO Jean Hu said, "We expect revenue to be approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. The middle point of our guidance represents approximately 66% year-over-year revenue growth, primarily driven by the acceleration of our Data Center segment." AMD says its Q4 revenue projections are up another 27 percent from this quarter's results. As reported by Tom's Hardware , Intel's Q4 guidance places revenue estimates between $15 and $16 billion. That means that if both companies land where they expect to at the end of the fourth quarter, AMD would exceed Intel's revenue for the first time in history. The data center segment of AMD's business was up 97 percent year over year, with a record $8.5 billion. AMD attributes the growth to demand for its EPYC line of enterprise server CPUs, along with the launch of the Instinct MI450 series GPUs . items.title: فالفيردي بعد هدفه القاتل: من دواعي سروري اللعب تحت قيادة هذا الجهاز الفني
items.summary: "لن نتوقف أبداً عن المحاولة"
items.body: "لن نتوقف أبداً عن المحاولة" كشف فيديركو فالفيردي، نجم ريال مدريد، سر ريمونتادا الفريق الملكي، أمام مضيفه آيك أثينا اليوناني، مساء اليوم الأربعاء. وحوّل ريال مدريد تأخره أمام مضيفه آيك أثينا اليوناني إلى انتصار قاتل وثمين بنتيجة 3-2 في المباراة التي جرت مساء اليوم الأربعاء، ضمن الجولة الرابعة من مرحلة الدوري بدوري أبطال أوروبا. وسجل فالفيردي، هدف فوز ريال مدريد في الدقيقة 90+2 ليمنح الملكي 3 نقاط ثمينة. وقال فالفيردي في تصريحات عبر شبكة " موفيستار ": "كانت مباراة صعبة ومعقدة. أعتقد أننا سيطرنا على مجريات اللعب. أهنئ الفريق على جهوده". وواصل: "أثر هدفهم الأول علينا.. واصل الفريق لعبه المعتاد والعمل الذي قمنا به خلال الأسبوع. استعدنا السيطرة، وشعرنا بالراحة مجدداً. بدأنا الهجوم مرة أخرى وبذلنا نفس الجهد الذي كنا نبذله". وحول قلب الطاولة على آيك، أوضح قائد ريال مدريد: "يعود الفضل إلى الجهاز التدريبي واللاعبين لاستمرارهم في الثقة بزملائهم". ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة وتابع: "إنه لمن دواعي سروري اللعب تحت قيادة هذا الجهاز التدريبي. لن نتوقف أبداً عن المحاولة". وعن هدف الفوز الذي سجله في الثواني الأخيرة، علق: "أحياناً أفكر في الأمر كثيراً. أنا ممتن لزملائي في الفريق الذين يمنحونني الثقة للمحاولة".

items.title: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”
items.summary: Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.
items.body: Donald Trump’s big, rapid American AI buildout now faces a major slowdown as voters in yesterday’s elections overwhelmingly supported candidates and measures that favored increasing restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide. One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects. In addition to increasing regulations on data centers, voters also backed anti-AI candidates, electing officials vowing crackdowns in key states building out the most data center capacity in the US. items.title: After Texas' blue wave, what happens to Elon Musk and SpaceX?
items.summary: "Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now."
items.body: Following his public disputes with California authorities during the COVID-19 pandemic, Elon Musk personally moved to Texas, outside of Austin, in 2020. Over the next six years, he doubled down on the Lone Star State. In 2021, Musk increasingly focused the Starship program in South Texas, urging SpaceX employees to move there and work on the company's future. In March of that year, he began using the name Starbase to describe the production and launch facilities near the Rio Grande River. In 2023, he built a massive factory east of Austin to manufacture customer terminals and other electronics for the Starlink program. In July 2024, he announced that SpaceX would relocate its corporate headquarters from Hawthorne, California, to Starbase, Texas. He cited California's regulatory and political environment as the motivating factor. Read full article Comments

items.body: The hackers who stole billions of dollars in cryptocurrency from the Binance exchange spent months working on the theft and used both social engineering and novel malware in the process, the company said Tuesday. The heist, which both the FBI and the TRM Security firm attributed to North Korean actors, initially targeted $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance wallets. The exchange has since frozen or intercepted $2.85 billion of that sum. Binance said it has set aside funds required to cover the loss and provided this link to a Proof of Reserves page. The $6.34 billion represents the biggest sum ever targeted in a cryptocurrency theft. Advanced persistent threat Binance said the people behind the heist began no later than June and continued until last Thursday, when they successfully compromised an engineer's laptop and withdrew assets from several wallets. Like just about every organization that suffers a public, high-consequence hack, Binance said the threat actor was sophisticated and resourceful. Read full article Comments

items.title: What I learned driving the Slate electric truck prototype
items.summary: After 45 minutes behind the wheel, I am more optimistic about the $25,000 EV.
items.body: If my 45-minute drive yesterday morning is anything to go by, I think Slate Auto will have quite the hit on its hands. The startup had one of its prototype trucks in town and asked if I wanted to check it out—no jumping on a plane or having to spend yet another night in an interchangeable hotel room, just a drive from southwest DC to Rockville, Maryland. Easy-peasy. The prototype truck had been well-used, with almost 6,000 miles (9,656 km) showing on the small and minimalist but very legible digital display that also shows your speed and, if you engage reverse, the backup camera. And while the cabin layout was representative of the production version, the surfaces most certainly weren’t—the prototype instead uses a lot of hard and shiny black plastic, with strips of Velcro here and there left over from when the interior had to be camouflaged when the vehicle was out in public. Getting acquainted with the Slate was refreshingly easy. The Morris Marina-like door handles open with a pleasing mechanical action. The seat and steering column adjust manually but with plenty of reach, something many budget models used to leave out to save on cost. Read full article Comments

items.title: The DEA banned a drug some opioid users called a miracle
items.summary: Researchers say the Schedule I ban could kill studies of a promising opioid treatment.
items.body: In 2012, as the driver of deaths in the opioid crisis began moving from prescription pills to heroin, Laura Bohn was tasked with finding safer drugs to manage pain. Funded by the National Institute on Drug Abuse, in 2017 she and other scientists revealed in the science journal Cell that several compounds—including a particularly promising one called SR-17018—could relieve pain in mice without causing respiratory depression. That’s a big deal, because respiratory depression is typically what causes people using opioids to stop breathing and die. Bohn, senior associate vice president of research at University of South Florida Health, says her team filed a patent on SR-17018. They went on to discover that mice using the chemical did not develop a high tolerance for it and that mice already dependent on morphine—a powerful opioid—could consume SR-17018 to reset their tolerance without suffering from painful withdrawal symptoms. "Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere," the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Citing third-party revenue estimates, the suit claimed that "Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission," while "publishers have received nothing." The lawsuit said, "AI companies pay Brave to provide them with real-time online content from the Brave search index," and use content from the Brave index "to train their own AI models" and "to respond to specific user queries." Google's new overarching approach to AI in K-12 classrooms sounds good on the surface. After consulting educators, researchers, and lawmakers, Google has decided that schools using its education products will be opted out of AI tools by default. It will be up to administrators to manually enable them when these changes roll out in the coming months. When you look at what Google considers to be an AI tool, the nature of the Faustian bargain becomes clear. The affected products are Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search . items.title: UEFI bootkit infected fully patched Windows machines. Is Microsoft to blame?
items.summary: UEFI bootkit BlackX exploits Microsoft's lack of clarity around Secure Boot protections.
items.body: In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in-the-wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. With the industry-wide chain-of-trust mechanism subverted, the malware was able to run malicious code before Windows was fully loaded and many security defenses were operational. Microsoft had already patched the vulnerability that BlackLotus exploited in 2022. In 2023 and 2024, Microsoft issued additional updates. The first added a new certificate that no longer trusted the vulnerable boot managers. The second provided the means to revoke trust in the digital certificate used to sign older vulnerable Windows boot managers. The organizations infected by the new bootkit, which is tracked under the name BlackX, had installed all of these patches. So how did they fall victim? UEFI bootkit refresher Before discussing the incident further, a brief review of BlackLotus and UEFI malware is in order. Short for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface , UEFI is firmware that runs immediately after a computer is turned on.
